verdict.P1 the pitch and the demand: PASS. Crossovers serve one INTERFACE every 32 bp = 10.88 nm, so a hinge line of n crossovers demands (n-1) x 10.88 nm of collinear interface. Sixteen demands 163.2 nm.
verdict.P2 does a 16-crossover hinge line exist: FAIL, at every one of the 32 phases and in BOTH directions of the sheet. The largest hinge line a 40 nm tile carries is FOUR, at every phase; the other parity carries three at the 22 seven-column phases and four at the 10 eight-column ones. Sixteen needs 163.2 nm of collinear interface (4.08 tiles) longitudinally, or 33 duplexes = 88.8 nm (2.22 tiles) transversally - and the transverse line restrains the wrong axis in any case. The absolute geometric ceiling, a line spanning the tile dilated by its own arm, is SIX.
verdict.the best and worst phases: The 10 centro-symmetric eight-column phases - [6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26] bp - carry FOUR on BOTH parities. The other 22 carry four on one parity and three on the other, so a hinge line placed on the wrong parity there loses 25 %. The phases that maximise the hinge line are exactly C-0015's centro-symmetric ones, and nothing in either construction forced that.
verdict.P3 upstream: PASS. The census reproduces C-0015 exactly: 56 crossovers at 10 phases, 49 at 22, 10 centro-symmetric phases, and it agrees with CrossoverLayout itself at every phase with departure 0.0.
verdict.P4 what the design does at the count tha: FAIL. C-0034's pipeline needs 10 crossovers to place an arm long enough to lift 10 nm by rotation, 12 for a design that also holds C-0023's ceiling at that stroke, and 3 to hold the 40 pN/nm ceiling at the acceptable stroke. The lattice supplies 4 on a full-length tile interface, 6 at the absolute geometric ceiling, and 2 per flexure at 45 paths. At four crossovers the arm places at 7.748 nm - sec 3's acceptable 3 nm stroke clears with a tangent of 36.58 pN/nm inside the ceiling, and the desired 10 nm stroke is out of geometric reach. At the one or two crossovers 45 independent flexures can each own, the tangent is 42.01-54.11 pN/nm, past C-0023's own ceiling, so even the ACCEPTABLE stroke fails.
verdict.P5 the conflict with C-0015's 45 attachm: FAIL, and it is arithmetic. The whole tile carries 49-56 crossovers; 45 paths at 16 demand 720, which is 12.86x every crossover the sheet has. Even at ONE crossover per flexure the demand is 45 against 49-56 - 80-92 % of the inventory - and every one of those crossovers is already a structural load path in C-0009's and C-0015's grillage. The 3 x 15 grid and a 16-crossover hinge cannot be built on the same sheet.
verdict.P6 the continuum control: PASS, and it settles what kind of fact this is. A continuum hinge line of the same length carries 3.676 crossovers of density, so the lattice quantisation is worth -18 % to +9 % - while the assertion is out by 4.35x. The verdict is a CONTINUUM fact about crossover density, not a quantisation artefact. The fan's own discreteness is likewise bounded: 6.0x at one interface, 1.47x at four, 1 + 3/(2m) asymptotically.
verdict.where sixteen crossovers CAN be found, a: Sixteen crossovers can be ASSEMBLED into one flexure - four interfaces of four is exactly sixteen - but interfaces compose in SERIES, not in parallel, because each carries only the moment of what is outboard of it and turns through its own angle. n_eff = n_i x 3(2m-1)/(m(2m+1)), so sixteen crossovers in that arrangement are worth 2.333 of hinge - 14.6 % of their own count - on a lever of 9.415 nm, and 45 of them assemble to 16.03 pN/nm, 2.08x too soft for the mandate.
verdict.maturity: TRL 1-3. A COUNT on a lattice whose pitch is cited and measured. Nothing here is measured, no sheet has been built, and no routing here is a sequence design. The rigid-raft census is an UPPER bound on participation: C-0009's own result is that a point load is carried by its two nearest crossovers and essentially nothing else, so the realised count runs lower, never higher.
